name: Computer Science
notes: For Columbia College students declaring in Spring 2024 or later. Students who declared earlier should check their cohort’s requirements.
ENGI E1006 or COMS W1002 is optional introductory preparation.
Up to 6 points of supervised projects or thesis may count. Credit for this purpose requires at least 3 points in a single enrollment.

The department restricts overlap among equivalent data structures, linear algebra, probability, and machine learning courses. Unused area foundation courses can count as electives if they satisfy the elective rule.
publishedCredits: 44–56 points across the four published component ranges

groups.label: Multivariable calculus
groups.note: Calculus III requires Calculus I. The accelerated and engineering alternatives require Calculus I and II, or equivalent preparation.

groups.label: Linear algebra and probability
groups.note: MATH UN2015 covers both subjects. The alternative uses two courses, one in linear algebra and one in probability or statistics.

groups.label: Introductory programming
groups.note: A score of 4 or 5 on AP Computer Science A can provide 3 points and an exemption from COMS W1004. The Bulletin lists COMS W1007 as the honors alternative.

groups.label: Upper-level CS electives
groups.note: Choose distinct COMS or jointly listed CS courses numbered 3000 or higher, including Barnard CS. Each enrollment must earn at least 3 points. The menu lists cataloged options with a course description, scheduled section, or explicit program listing. Future and special-topic offerings vary. Up to 6 points of supervised projects or thesis may count. Credit for this purpose requires at least 3 points in a single enrollment.
